sanskrit: aiśvaryamadapāpiṣṭhā madāḥ pānamadādayaḥ aiśvaryamadamatto hi nāpatitvā vibudhyate
english: The intoxications of power are the most sinful of intoxications — the pride of drinking and the rest. For one intoxicated by the pride of power does not recover his senses until he has fallen.

sanskrit: indriyair indriyārtheṣu vartamānair anigrahaiḥ tair ayaṃ tāpyate loko nakṣatrāṇi grahair iva
english: By the senses, ungoverned, roaming among their objects, this world is afflicted, even as the stars are afflicted by the planets.

sanskrit: yo jitaḥ pañcavargeṇa sahajenātmakarśinā āpadas tasya vardhante śuklapakṣa ivoḍurāṭ
english: He who is conquered by the fivefold group of senses that are innate and tormenting of the self — his calamities grow like the moon in the bright fortnight.

sanskrit: avijitya ya ātmānam amātyān vijigīṣate amitrān vājitāmātyaḥ so 'vaśaḥ parihīyate
english: He who, without having conquered himself, desires to conquer his ministers and his enemies, without having subdued his ministers, becomes powerless and comes to ruin.

sanskrit: ātmānam eva prathamaṃ deśarūpeṇa yo jayet tato 'mātyān amitrāṃś ca na moghaṃ vijigīṣate
english: He who first conquers himself by fitting means, and thereafter his ministers and his enemies — his desire for conquest does not go in vain.

sanskrit: vaśyendriyaṃ jitāmātyaṃ dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ vikāriṣu parīkṣyakāriṇaṃ dhīram atyantaṃ śrīr niṣevate
english: He whose senses are subdued, whose ministers are conquered, who applies punishment with firmness against offenders, who acts after deliberation and is steadfast — upon such a one prosperity eternally waits.

sanskrit: rathaḥ śarīraṃ puruṣasya rājan; nātmā niyantendriyāṇy asya cāśvāḥ tair apramattaḥ kuśalaḥ sadaśvair; dāntaiḥ sukhaṃ yāti rathīva dhīraḥ
english: O king, the body of a man is his chariot; the self is not the driver — his senses are the horses. Vigilant and skilled, with good and well-trained horses, the steadfast man travels comfortably, like a charioteer.

sanskrit: etāny anigṛhītāni vyāpādayitum apy alam avidheyā ivādāntā hayāḥ pathi kusārathim
english: These senses, if ungoverned, are capable of killing a man, like unruly untamed horses on the road that destroy a poor charioteer.

sanskrit: anartham arthataḥ paśyann arthaṃ caivāpy anarthataḥ indriyaiḥ prasṛto bālaḥ suduḥkhaṃ manyate sukham
english: The fool, led astray by the senses, sees harm as benefit and benefit as harm; he regards great suffering as pleasure.

sanskrit: dharmārthau yaḥ parityajya syād indriyavaśānugaḥ śrīprāṇadhanadārebhya kṣipraṃ sa parihīyate
english: He who, abandoning righteousness and worldly good, follows in the wake of his senses — he quickly comes to ruin in respect of prosperity, life, wealth, and wife.

sanskrit: arthānām īśvaro yaḥ syād indriyāṇām anīśvaraḥ indriyāṇām anaiśvaryād aiśvaryād bhraśyate hi saḥ
english: He who is master of wealth but not master of his senses — from the lack of mastery over his senses he falls from that very mastery of wealth.

sanskrit: ātmanātmānam anvicchen manobuddhīndriyair yataiḥ ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
english: One should seek the self by the self, with mind, intellect, and senses disciplined; for the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.

sanskrit: kṣudrākṣeṇeva jālena jhaṣāv apihitāv ubhau kāmaś ca rājan krodhaś ca tau prajñānaṃ vilumpataḥ
english: O king, desire and anger — those two, like fish trapped in a net with small meshes — rob a person of his wisdom.

sanskrit: samavekṣyeha dharmārthau saṃbhārān yo 'dhigacchati sa vai saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāraḥ satataṃ sukham edhate
english: He who, having duly considered righteousness and worldly good in this world, acquires the means for both — he who has gathered the proper means thrives in happiness always.

sanskrit: yaḥ pañcābhyantarāñ śatrūn avijitya matikṣayān jigīṣati ripūn anyān ripavo 'bhibhavanti tam
english: He who, without conquering the five inner enemies that destroy the mind, desires to conquer external foes — those very enemies overcome him.

sanskrit: dṛśyante hi durātmāno vadhyamānāḥ svakarmabhiḥ indriyāṇām anīśatvād rājāno rājyavibhramaiḥ
english: Indeed, evil-souled kings are seen being slain by their own deeds, losing their kingdoms through lack of mastery over the senses.

sanskrit: asaṃtyāgāt pāpakṛtām apāpāṃs; tulyo daṇḍaḥ spṛśate miśrabhāvāt śuṣkeṇārdraṃ dahyate miśrabhāvāt; tasmāt pāpaiḥ saha saṃdhiṃ na kuryāt
english: Because of not abandoning the company of evil-doers, punishment touches the innocent equally, through association. Because of mixing with the dry, the moist is burned; therefore one should never make alliance with the wicked.

sanskrit: nijān utpatataḥ śatrūn pañca pañcaprayojanān yo mohān na nigṛhṇāti tam āpad grasate naram
english: The man who, through delusion, does not restrain the five arising inner enemies — each with its five effects — him calamity devours.

sanskrit: anasūyārjavaṃ śaucaṃ saṃtoṣaḥ priyavāditā damaḥ satyam anāyāso na bhavanti durātmanām
english: Freedom from envy, straightforwardness, purity, contentment, pleasant speech, self-restraint, truthfulness, and ease of conduct — these do not belong to the evil-natured.

sanskrit: ātmajñānam anāyāsas titikṣā dharmanityatā vāk caiva guptā dānaṃ ca naitāny antyeṣu bhārata
english: Self-knowledge, ease of conduct, forbearance, constant adherence to duty, guarded speech, and generosity — O Bhārata, these are not found among the lowest.

sanskrit: ākrośaparivādābhyāṃ vihiṃsanty abudhā budhān vaktā pāpam upādatte kṣamamāṇo vimucyate
english: The ignorant injure the wise through abuse and slander; the speaker acquires sin, while the one who forgives is set free.

sanskrit: hiṃsā balam asādhūnāṃ rājñāṃ daṇḍavidhir balam śuśrūṣā tu balaṃ strīṇāṃ kṣamā guṇavatāṃ balam
english: Violence is the strength of the wicked; the application of punishment is the strength of kings; service is the strength of women; forbearance is the strength of the virtuous.

sanskrit: vāksaṃyamo hi nṛpate suduṣkaratamo mataḥ arthavac ca vicitraṃ ca na śakyaṃ bahu bhāṣitum
english: O king, restraint of speech is considered the most difficult of all disciplines; to speak what is meaningful and varied at length is not possible.

sanskrit: abhyāvahati kalyāṇaṃ vividhā vāk subhāṣitā saiva durbhāṣitā rājann anarthāyopapadyate
english: Various kinds of well-spoken speech bring auspiciousness; that same speech, ill-spoken, O king, leads only to harm.

sanskrit: saṃrohati śarair viddhaṃ vanaṃ paraśunā hatam vācā duruktaṃ bībhatsaṃ na saṃrohati vākkṣatam
english: A forest pierced by arrows heals; one felled by an axe heals. But a wound inflicted by ugly speech does not heal — a wound made by words does not close.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkanārācā nirharanti śarīrataḥ vākśalyas tu na nirhartuṃ śakyo hṛdiśayo hi saḥ
english: Barbed arrows, reeds, and iron shafts can be removed from the body; but the dart of speech cannot be removed — for it lodges in the heart.

sanskrit: vāksāyakā vadanān niṣpatanti; yair āhataḥ śocati rātryahāni parasya nāmarmasu te patanti; tān paṇḍito nāvasṛjet pareṣu
english: Word-arrows fly from the mouth; struck by them, another grieves by night and by day. They do not fall on the vital spots of others alone — the wise man should not release them against others.

sanskrit: yasmai devāḥ prayacchanti puruṣāya parābhavam buddhiṃ tasyāpakarṣanti so 'pācīnāni paśyati
english: When the gods wish to bring a man to ruin, they first take away his understanding; he then perceives all things inversely.

sanskrit: buddhau kaluṣabhūtāyāṃ vināśe pratyupasthite anayo nayasaṃkāśo hṛdayān nāpasarpati
english: When the intellect has become turbid and destruction is imminent, wrong policy, wearing the appearance of right policy, does not depart from the heart.

sanskrit: seyaṃ buddhiḥ parītā te putrāṇāṃ tava bhārata pāṇḍavānāṃ virodhena na cainām avabudhyase
english: Such, O Bhārata, is the understanding that has seized you — through hostility to your sons, the Pāṇḍavas — and you do not perceive it.

sanskrit: rājā lakṣaṇasaṃpannas trailokyasyāpi yo bhavet śiṣyas te śāsitā so 'stu dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, let Yudhiṣṭhira — who is endowed with kingly qualities and could be king of all three worlds — be your pupil and rule under your guidance.

sanskrit: atīva sarvān putrāṃs te bhāgadheyapuraskṛtaḥ tejasā prajñayā caiva yukto dharmārthatattvavit
english: He surpasses all your sons in fortune, endowed with splendor and wisdom, and knowing the truth of righteousness and worldly good.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyād anukrośād yo 'sau dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ gauravāt tava rājendra bahūn kleśāṃs titikṣati
english: He who is the foremost among the upholders of righteousness, by virtue of compassion and mercy, O king of kings, endures many sufferings out of reverence for you.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca brūhi bhūyo mahābuddhe dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ śṛṇvato nāsti me tṛptir vicitrāṇīha bhāṣase
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Speak again, O great intellect, words that accord with righteousness and worldly good. Listening to you, I am not satisfied — you speak such varied and wondrous things.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca sarvatīrtheṣu vā snānaṃ sarvabhūteṣu cārjavam ubhe ete same syātām ārjavaṃ vā viśiṣyate
english: Vidura said: Bathing at all sacred fords, and straightforwardness toward all beings — these two may be regarded as equal; or rather, straightforwardness is superior.

sanskrit: ārjavaṃ pratipadyasva putreṣu satataṃ vibho iha kīrtiṃ parāṃ prāpya pretya svargam avāpsyasi
english: Adopt straightforwardness toward your sons always, O lord; having gained the highest fame here, you shall obtain heaven hereafter.

sanskrit: yāvat kīrtir manuṣyasya puṇyā lokeṣu gīyate tāvat sa puruṣavyāghra svargaloke mahīyate
english: As long as a man's meritorious glory is sung in the worlds, O tiger among men, so long is he honored in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam virocanasya saṃvādaṃ keśinyarthe sudhanvanā
english: On this point they cite this ancient history — the dialogue between Virocana and Sudhanvan over Keśinī.

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca kiṃ brāhmaṇāḥ svic chreyāṃso ditijāḥ svid virocana atha kena sma paryaṅkaṃ sudhanvā nādhirohati
english: Keśinī said: Are Brāhmaṇas superior, or are the sons of Diti, O Virocana? And why does Sudhanvan not mount the couch?

sanskrit: virocana uvāca prājāpatyā hi vai śreṣṭhā vayaṃ keśini sattamāḥ asmākaṃ khalv ime lokāḥ ke devāḥ ke dvijātayaḥ
english: Virocana said: We, the offspring of Prajāpati, are indeed the foremost, O Keśinī, the best of beings. These worlds belong to us — what are the gods, what are the twice-born?

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca ihaivāssva pratīkṣāva upasthāne virocana sudhanvā prātar āgantā paśyeyaṃ vāṃ samāgatau
english: Keśinī said: Stay right here, let us wait in attendance, O Virocana — Sudhanvan will come in the morning; I wish to see you two together.

sanskrit: virocana uvāca tathā bhadre kariṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ bhīru bhāṣase sudhanvānaṃ ca māṃ caiva prātar draṣṭāsi saṃgatau
english: Virocana said: So shall I do, O gracious one, as you, O timid one, say; in the morning you shall see both Sudhanvan and me together.

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca anvālabhe hiraṇmayaṃ prāhrāde 'haṃ tavāsanam ekatvam upasaṃpanno na tv āseyaṃ tvayā saha
english: Sudhanvan said: I touch your golden seat, O son of Prahlāda; I have come here alone, but I will not sit together with you.

sanskrit: virocana uvāca anvāharantu phalakaṃ kūrcaṃ vāpy atha vā bṛsīm sudhanvan na tvam arho 'si mayā saha samāsanam
english: Virocana said: Let them bring a plank, a bundle of grass, or a mat — O Sudhanvan, you are not worthy to sit together with me.

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca pitāpi te samāsīnam upāsītaiva mām adhaḥ bālaḥ sukhaidhito gehe na tvaṃ kiṃ cana budhyase
english: Sudhanvan said: Even your father would attend upon me seated beside him from below. You are a child, reared in comfort at home — you understand nothing.

sanskrit: virocana uvāca hiraṇyaṃ ca gavāśvaṃ ca yad vittam asureṣu naḥ sudhanvan vipaṇe tena praśnaṃ pṛcchāva ye viduḥ
english: Virocana said: O Sudhanvan, let us wager all the gold, cattle, and horses that are our wealth among the asuras, and then let those who know arbitrate our question.

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca hiraṇyaṃ ca gavāśvaṃ ca tavaivāstu virocana prāṇayos tu paṇaṃ kṛtvā praśnaṃ pṛcchāva ye viduḥ
english: Sudhanvan said: Let the gold, cattle, and horses be yours, O Virocana. But let us wager our very lives and then ask those who know to arbitrate.

sanskrit: virocana uvāca āvāṃ kutra gamiṣyāvaḥ prāṇayor vipaṇe kṛte na hi deveṣv ahaṃ sthātā na manuṣyeṣu karhi cit
english: Virocana said: Where shall we two go, with our lives as the stake? I would not stand among the gods, nor among humans at any time.

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca pitaraṃ te gamiṣyāvaḥ prāṇayor vipaṇe kṛte putrasyāpi sa hetor hi prahrādo nānṛtaṃ vadet
english: Sudhanvan said: We shall go to your father, with our lives as the stake; for even for the sake of his son, Prahlāda would not speak falsehood.

sanskrit: prahrāda uvāca imau tau saṃpradṛśyete yābhyāṃ na caritaṃ saha āśīviṣāv iva kruddhāv ekamārgam ihāgatau
english: Prahlāda said: These two appear before me — who have not walked together — come here by the same road like two angry venomous serpents.

sanskrit: kiṃ vai sahaiva carato na purā carataḥ saha virocanaitat pṛcchāmi kiṃ te sakhyaṃ sudhanvanā
english: Why do they come together now who did not walk together before? O Virocana, I ask you this: what is your friendship with Sudhanvan?

sanskrit: virocana uvāca na me sudhanvanā sakhyaṃ prāṇayor vipaṇāvahe prahrāda tat tvāṃ pṛcchāmi mā praśnam anṛtaṃ vadīḥ
english: Virocana said: There is no friendship between Sudhanvan and me — we have wagered our lives. O Prahlāda, I ask you this: do not speak falsely in answering.

sanskrit: prahrāda uvāca udakaṃ madhuparkaṃ cāpy ānayantu sudhanvane brahmann abhyarcanīyo 'si śvetā gauḥ pīvarīkṛtā
english: Prahlāda said: Let water and honey-mixture be brought for Sudhanvan. O Brahmin, you are worthy of honor; a white, well-nourished cow shall be given.

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca udakaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca patha evārpitaṃ mama prahrāda tvaṃ tu nau praśnaṃ tathyaṃ prabrūhi pṛcchatoḥ
english: Sudhanvan said: Water and honey-mixture have already been offered to me on the road. O Prahlāda, please speak the truth in answer to our question.

sanskrit: prahrāda uvāca putro vānyo bhavān brahman sākṣye caiva bhavet sthitaḥ tayor vivadatoḥ praśnaṃ katham asmadvidho vadet
english: Prahlāda said: O Brahmin, either my son or you would be placed in the position of a witness. How can one like me speak to the question of two who are in dispute?

sanskrit: atha yo naiva prabrūyāt satyaṃ vā yadi vānṛtam etat sudhanvan pṛcchāmi durvivaktā sma kiṃ vaset
english: Now, O Sudhanvan, I ask you this: one who would speak neither truth nor falsehood — where does such a poor witness dwell?

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca yāṃ rātrim adhivinnā strī yāṃ caivākṣaparājitaḥ yāṃ ca bhārābhitaptāṅgo durvivaktā sma tāṃ vaset
english: Sudhanvan said: The same night as a woman whose husband has taken another wife, as a man defeated at dice, as one whose limbs are exhausted from bearing a heavy load — in that same condition does the poor witness dwell.

sanskrit: nagare pratiruddhaḥ san bahirdvāre bubhukṣitaḥ amitrān bhūyasaḥ paśyan durvivaktā sma tāṃ vaset
english: Shut out in a city, hungry outside the gate, seeing his enemies in the majority — in that condition does the poor witness dwell.

sanskrit: pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte śatam aśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte
english: Lying about animals kills five; lying about cows kills ten; lying about horses kills a hundred; lying about a man kills a thousand.

sanskrit: hanti jātān ajātāṃś ca hiraṇyārthe 'nṛtaṃ vadan sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛte hanti mā sma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadīḥ
english: Lying for the sake of gold kills those already born and those yet unborn; lying about land destroys everything — therefore never speak falsehood about land.

sanskrit: prahrāda uvāca mattaḥ śreyān aṅgirā vai sudhanvā tvad virocana mātāsya śreyasī mātus tasmāt tvaṃ tena vai jitaḥ
english: Prahlāda said: Sudhanvan, born of Aṅgiras, is superior to me, O Virocana; his mother is superior to your mother. Therefore you are indeed defeated by him.

sanskrit: virocana sudhanvāyaṃ prāṇānām īśvaras tava sudhanvan punar icchāmi tvayā dattaṃ virocanam
english: O Virocana, Sudhanvan is now the master of your life. But O Sudhanvan, I desire that Virocana be given back by you.

sanskrit: sudhanvovāca yad dharmam avṛṇīthās tvaṃ na kāmād anṛtaṃ vadīḥ punar dadāmi te tasmāt putraṃ prahrāda durlabham
english: Sudhanvan said: Because you chose righteousness and did not speak falsehood out of desire, therefore I give back to you your son, O Prahlāda — the one hard to obtain.

sanskrit: eṣa prahrāda putras te mayā datto virocanaḥ pādaprakṣālanaṃ kuryāt kumāryāḥ saṃnidhau mama
english: This Virocana, your son, O Prahlāda, is given back by me. Let him wash the feet of the maiden in my presence.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca tasmād rājendra bhūmyarthe nānṛtaṃ vaktum arhasi mā gamaḥ sasutāmātyo 'tyayaṃ putrān anubhraman
english: Vidura said: Therefore, O king of kings, you should not speak falsehood for the sake of land. Do not lead yourself with sons and ministers to ruin while pursuing your sons.

sanskrit: na devā yaṣṭim ādāya rakṣanti paśupālavat yaṃ tu rakṣitum icchanti buddhyā saṃvibhajanti tam
english: The gods do not protect one with a staff in hand, as a cowherd guards cattle; rather, him whom they wish to protect they endow with wisdom.

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇe kurute manaḥ tathā tathāsya sarvārthāḥ sidhyante nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: In the exact measure that a man sets his mind on virtue, in that measure all his purposes succeed — there is no doubt in this.

sanskrit: na chandāṃsi vṛjināt tārayanti; māyāvinaṃ māyayā vartamānam nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāś; chandāṃsy enaṃ prajahaty antakāle
english: The sacred hymns do not save the deceitful man who lives by deceit from his sins; as fledglings leave the nest once their wings have grown, the sacred hymns abandon him at the time of death.

sanskrit: mattāpānaṃ kalahaṃ pūgavairaṃ; bhāryāpatyor antaraṃ jñātibhedam rājadviṣṭaṃ strīpumāṃsor vivādaṃ; varjyāny āhur yaś ca panthāḥ praduṣṭaḥ
english: Drinking in a state of intoxication, quarrel, enmity with a guild, dispute between husband and wife, estrangement from kinsmen, acting against the king's wishes, controversy between men and women — these are to be avoided, as is a corrupt path.

sanskrit: sāmudrikaṃ vaṇijaṃ corapūrvaṃ; śalākadhūrtaṃ ca cikitsakaṃ ca ariṃ ca mitraṃ ca kuśīlavaṃ ca; naitān sākṣyeṣv adhikurvīta sapta
english: A soothsayer, a merchant, a former thief, a dice-cheat, a physician, an enemy, and a friend — these seven one should not employ as witnesses.

sanskrit: mānāgnihotram uta mānamaunaṃ; mānenādhītam uta mānayajñaḥ etāni catvāry abhayaṃkarāṇi; bhayaṃ prayacchanty ayathākṛtāni
english: An agnihotra performed out of pride, silence practiced out of pride, learning studied out of pride, and sacrifice performed out of pride — these four, which should bring fearlessness, bring fear when performed in the wrong spirit.

sanskrit: agāradāhī garadaḥ kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī parvakāraś ca sūcī ca mitradhruk pāradārikaḥ
english: An arsonist, a poisoner, one who eats from a paramour's household, a seller of soma, a maker of impure festivals, an informer, one who betrays friends, and an adulterer —

sanskrit: bhrūṇahā gurutalpī ca yaś ca syāt pānapo dvijaḥ atitīkṣṇaś ca kākaś ca nāstiko vedanindakaḥ
english: — a slayer of an embryo, one who violates his guru's bed, a Brahmin who drinks liquor, an excessively harsh person, a crow-natured person, an atheist, and a reviler of the Vedas —

sanskrit: sruvapragrahaṇo vrātyaḥ kīnāśaś cārthavān api rakṣety uktaś ca yo hiṃsyāt sarve brahmahaṇaiḥ samāḥ
english: — one who seizes the sacrificial ladle, an outcaste, a miser even if wealthy, and one who harms what he was told to protect — all these are equal to slayers of Brahmins.

sanskrit: tṛṇolkayā jñāyate jātarūpaṃ; yuge bhadro vyavahāreṇa sādhuḥ śūro bhayeṣv arthakṛcchreṣu dhīraḥ; kṛcchrāsv āpatsu suhṛdaś cārayaś ca
english: Gold is tested by a fire of grass; a good one is tested by conduct in the yoke of life; a hero is tested by fearful and financially distressing situations; and in grave calamities, friends and enemies alike are tested.

sanskrit: jarā rūpaṃ harati hi dhairyam āśā; mṛtyuḥ prāṇān dharmacaryām asūyā krodhaḥ śriyaṃ śīlam anāryasevā; hriyaṃ kāmaḥ sarvam evābhimānaḥ
english: Old age steals beauty; hope steals steadiness of mind; death takes away life; envy destroys righteous conduct; anger destroys prosperity; association with the ignoble destroys character; lust destroys modesty; and pride destroys everything.

sanskrit: śrīr maṅgalāt prabhavati prāgalbhyāt saṃpravardhate dākṣyāt tu kurute mūlaṃ saṃyamāt pratitiṣṭhati
english: Prosperity springs from auspiciousness; it grows further through boldness; it takes root through skill; and it becomes established through self-restraint.

sanskrit: aṣṭau guṇāḥ puruṣaṃ dīpayanti; prajñā ca kaulyaṃ ca damaḥ śrutaṃ ca parākramaś cābahubhāṣitā ca; dānaṃ yathāśakti kṛtajñatā ca
english: Eight qualities illuminate a man: wisdom, noble birth, self-control, learning, valor, speaking little, generosity according to one's ability, and gratitude.

sanskrit: etān guṇāṃs tāta mahānubhāvān; eko guṇaḥ saṃśrayate prasahya rājā yadā satkurute manuṣyaṃ; sarvān guṇān eṣa guṇo 'tibhāti
english: All these great and glorious qualities are subsumed by one quality that overwhelms them: when a king honors a person, that single quality outshines all other qualities.

sanskrit: aṣṭau nṛpemāni manuṣyaloke; svargasya lokasya nidarśanāni catvāry eṣām anvavetāni sadbhiś; catvāry eṣām anvavayanti santaḥ
english: O king, these eight things in the world of men are manifestations of the world of heaven; four of these are followed by the good, and four of these are pursued by the righteous.
